newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP approves new data protection directive.
newsitem.headline: EP approves new data protection directive.

text.p: The European Parliament gave a second reading on Thursday to a draft directive which sets specific data protection rules for the European Union telecommunications sector.
Directive COM(94)128, which has taken six years to finalise, is designed to safeguard privacy and personal information in the liberalised telecoms market.
It gives subscribers the right not to receive unsolicited calls by telephone salesmen, and to go ex-directory.
Parliament deleted from the text approved by EU telecoms ministers in mid-1996 a provision allowing telephone companies to charge subscribers a small fee for this service.
Major companies developing services for the information superhighway have urged the EU to scrap the new directive.

The International Communications Round Table, which groups 30 leading publishing, media, computer and communications companies, says an existing, more general, directive on data protection -- 95/46/EEC -- provides sufficient cover.
